messages:
sam (runtime): Quick flag — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak on canary we saw a tail-latency bump in EU for short seq requests. p99 up ~30ms. Suspect cross-region spillover + KV cache churn. Anyone else seeing this?

maria (eng-ml): Yep, saw it in profiler. KV cache hit-rate for 1-8 token prefixes dropped from ~91% -> ~76% when requests spilled to partner cluster. Looks like different kernel choices changed internal sharding of KV keys.

vik (infra): Interesting. We had a soft-spill policy enabled for cross-region to avoid hot-spotting:
```
queue_policy: soft_spill
affinity: prefer_local
token_budget_us: 20000
spill_threshold_ms: 8
```
If kernel change changed per-request latency distribution, the spill trigger might be firing more often.

alex (eng-sre): Observed correlation between spill events and higher queue formation time. When spill happens we add ~5-10ms of network hop + scheduling. For short seqs that matters.

sam (runtime): So we need to decide: tune token_budget lower to keep more local, or relax affinity to reduce queuing hotspots? Both have tradeoffs. Lower token_budget -> more immediate dispatch (maybe less batching). Relax affinity -> more KV misses.

maria (eng-ml): From eval microbenchmarks: reducing token_budget_us from 20000 -> 12000 reduces p99 queuing by ~12ms but increases per-token CPU by ~2% due to smaller batches. KV hit-rate stays higher if we keep affinity.

anya (prod): Customer impact: two small EU customers reported slower responses on short completions yesterday. Not a large spike but noticeable for interactive flows. We should prioritize a quick mitigation.

vik (infra): Proposed quick mitigation: enable a regional hard-affinity shim for EU core traffic for next 2 hours, plus revert the kernel selector gating for canary. That should keep KV cache locality and reduce cross-region spill.

maria (eng-ml): Agreed for short-term. Longer-term we should update kernel selection to be alignment-aware with our KV sharding and add a cache-consistent hash fallback. Also add a metric for "spill-induced kv-miss-rate".

sam (runtime): Can we get a quick config to test? Something like:
```
queue_policy: regional_hard_affinity
affinity: hard
token_budget_us: 15000
spill_threshold_ms: 12
```
This keeps moderate batching but prevents cross-zone forwarding for EU routes.

vik (infra): I'll push a staged change to infra-config and route EU-prod traffic to the shim. deploy-bot: starting canary of config change.

deploy-bot: config-deploy starting: infra-config v2.14.2 -> rolling to eu clusters. Canary group=eu-small.

alex (eng-sre): After canary we should run a short p99 sweep:
- baseline: p50/p90/p99 before change
- post-change: same windows
Also collect KV hit-rate and spill count.

maria (eng-ml): I ran a simulated workload on staging with regional_hard_affinity + token_budget_us=15000: p99 down ~18ms vs canary baseline, KV hit-rate recovered to ~89%. Batch sizes decreased slightly but throughput unchanged for our latency-sensitive workloads.

sam (runtime): Nice. Let's proceed with the staged config and monitor. For the longer fix: I'll open a follow-up to make kernel-selector emit a KV-shard-stability score so the runtime can prefer kernels that keep KV key layout stable.

anya (prod): Keeping me posted for customer comms. If p99 stays high after the fix I'll trigger outreach.

vik (infra): Change rolled to canary; monitoring dashboards live. Will escalate to full rollout if no regression in 20m.

alex (eng-sre): Early canary numbers: eu-prod p99 back down ~22ms, spill events dropped 86%. Will watch the tail.

sam (runtime): Thanks. Follow-up todo: (1) kernel->kv stability metric, (2) add spill-induced-kv-miss ratio to console, (3) evaluate token_budget autoscaling based on in-flight seq length distribution.

maria (eng-ml): I'll add the dashboard tiles for kv-miss-by-spill and per-kernel kv-hit heatmap.

vik (infra): Rolling to full rollout in 5m.

deploy-bot: config-deploy success: infra-config v2.14.2 -> eu clusters.

sam (runtime): Early post-rollout check: p99 remains lower, customers reporting improved interactive latency. Closing this thread but logging follow-ups.

maria (eng-ml): Filing a small perf regression RCA with traces attached (will link in follow-up ticket).

anya (prod): Thanks team :thumbsup:
